transcript.text: Hi, I'm Mallika, and I'm jumping for the first time
since I had an ACL and meniscus surgery 8 months ago,
and since then I haven't jumped. [Original HI: aur tab se I have not jumped.]
I don't even remember what jumping feels like.
When I was fine, I took my knee for granted. [Original HI: Jab main theek thi, I took my knee for granted.]
I regret every time I could've jumped but didn't.
If I had known about my injury, that I won't be able to jump in the future, [Original HI: Agar mujhe meri injury ke baare mein pata hota, I won't be able to jump in the future,]
[partly unclear: she jokes she would have jumped everywhere] [Original HI: main kahi bhi... tumhe main...]
After warm-ups, I had to go through a few progressions to re-learn jumping. [Original HI: Warmup aur... I had to go through thodi progressions to re-learn jumping.]
After that, my physio said, 'Jump on this step.' [Original HI: Uske baad my physio said, jump on this step.]
I said, how, bro? How do I just jump like that? [Original HI: Aise kaise bhai? Aise kaise jump kar lu?]
Something I haven't done in 8 months, I'm scared, man. [Original HI: Jo cheez maine 8 mahine se nahi ki, meri fatt ti hai yaar.]
I don't wanna get hurt.
How can I tell my brain, 'Come on, jump'? [Original HI: How can I tell my brain, chalo jump?]
I was looking at that step, and it looked and felt impossible. [Original HI: Main us step ko dekh rahi thi, and it looked and felt impossible.]
I'd decided I couldn't do it. [Original HI: Main samajh gayi thi mere se nahi hone wala.]
Then I started to gaslight myself. [Original HI: Tab maine apne aap ko gaslight karna shuru kiya.]
How lame is it that you can't jump? Such an aura-minus move. [Original HI: Ye kitni... ki tu kud nahi sakti hai. Kitni aura minus wali harkat hai, that you can't jump.]
Everyone is watching you, have some shame. [Original HI: Sab log tujhe dekh rahe hain, thodi sharm kar.]
And that's when I jumped.
Wow.

hook.text: Hi, I'm Mallika, and I'm jumping for the first time
hook.template: I'm [DOING SOMETHING SIMPLE] for the first time since [SETBACK]
hook.whyItWorks: Jumping onto a low step sounds like nothing, so 'for the first time' creates an instant 'why is that a big deal?' gap. The answer arrives two seconds later with hospital-gown and walker footage, which turns a tiny movement into a comeback story people want to see finished.

format.visualLayout: Talking head at home in a striped tee and glasses, intercut with rehab-gym clips, hospital walker footage and the final jump; white captions with big pink keywords; black-and-white for the scared beats
format.pacing: fast, about 1 cut every 1.5 to 2s, with colour drops to black and white on emotional lines
format.reasoning: The story has a clear arc (injury, fear, self-talk, jump), so quick cuts between her telling it and the footage of each stage keep it moving. Comedy in the self-talk ('aura minus', 'thodi sharm kar') makes a vulnerable moment fun to share, and saving the jump for the last seconds holds people to the end.

angle.topic: Returning to exercise after ACL surgery
angle.angle: After rehab the last barrier is fear, and she talked herself past it
angle.commonBelief: Getting back after an injury is only about rebuilding strength
angle.contrarianTake: Your body can be ready before your brain is; the final step is mental

myVersion.hook: Your body is ready to train again. Your brain isn't. Let's talk about that.
myVersion.script:
Your body is ready to train again. Your brain isn't. Let's talk about that.
Maybe it's been two years since your baby.
Maybe your back gave out once and you've been scared to lift ever since.
Maybe you just stopped, and now the gym feels like a place for other people.
I see this with so many women who start with me.
We do the slow work first. Mobility. Light weights. Walking.
Week by week, the body gets stronger.
And then comes the day I ask for something new. A real squat with weight. A push-up from the floor.
And they freeze.
Not because they can't. Because they're scared they'll get hurt again.
That fear is real. It makes sense. Don't let anyone laugh at it.
But here's what I tell them.
Your strength is proof. You did the reps. You built this.
Fear is just your brain remembering the old you.
So we take a breath. We set up properly. I'm right there.
And they do it.
And every single time, the face after that first rep says everything.
If you're scared to start again, start smaller. But start.
Your body will remember faster than you think.
Comment READY if you're coming back this month.
